hints.content:
Let's examine the rotation of a single point, such as point $C$. This will tell us the angle of rotation, since all points undergo the same transformation.

Imagine a circle that passes through point $C$ with a center at point $P$.  What portion of the circle do we rotate through to reach the image? In which direction?

We need to rotate point $C$ through about $\dfrac{7}{24}$ of the circle to reach the image $C'$, so that is about $105^\circ$. 

![](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/578344cff8c97e47a719bdcb80089987ef2e0ecd)

Since we rotate *counterclockwise*, the angle of rotation is *positive*. That means point $C$ has an angle of rotation of $105^\circ$.
The angle of rotation for quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $105^\circ$.
